descent_claim: Karn's headers keep Rockliff's names (alpha_to, index_of, genpoly, the Lin-and-Costello table form) and generalise them; asserted from reading both bodies (Nyx, 2026-09-16), not from Techne's ancestry graph, which records no edge between them. Harmonia should treat the descent as a hypothesis the ruler tests, not a premise.

R-ID-1.input_class: random data blocks of 9 symbols, encoded by each body's own encoder
R-ID-1.expected: IDENTICAL parity symbols for every block (same generator polynomial from the same roots and field)
R-ID-1.if_not: either the parameter mapping above is wrong (Nyx's error) or the descent claim is wrong; either way the ruler has found something real -- record which

R-ID-2.input_class: codewords with 0..tt (=3) injected symbol errors at random positions
R-ID-2.expected: IDENTICAL corrected data from both decoders; a returns count of corrections via its own variables, b returns count via the function return
R-ID-2.if_not: descent claim wrong or a transcription error in one body

R-DIV-1.expected: DIVERGENCE: a passes the information symbols through UNCORRECTED with no flag (rs.c header text, lines 124-146 of the decoder comment: 'the information symbols as received are output'); b returns -1 (decode_rs.h count = -1 on locator-degree / root-count mismatch)
R-DIV-1.if_not: the ruler cannot see the one difference that is known by reading; it is not fit to adjudicate MECH-GZIP-LEVELTABLE-001 (whose I2 outcome differs from its CUT_KILL by 0.002 in ratio)

R-DIV-2.input_class: erasures (known positions) beyond tt errors but within 2tt total
R-DIV-2.expected: b corrects (erasure seeding, decode_rs.h 92-100); a has no erasure interface at all (header: 'does not handle erasures at present')
R-DIV-2.if_not: N/A -- a cannot be given erasures; this row records a capability asymmetry, not a behavioural divergence on shared inputs

what_a_broken_ruler_looks_like: scores R-ID-1/R-ID-2 as divergent (parameter mapping or normalisation defect), OR scores R-DIV-1 as identical (it is reading return codes only, or only correctable inputs were sampled), OR places libfec-karn::viterbi.* as close to a as b is (it is reading the domain label 'error-correcting-codes', not behaviour)

return_protocol.accountable_seat: Nyx receives the ruler's verdict on R-ID/R-DIV as CUT_SUPPORTED or CUT_CHALLENGE on the rs.* organs of both fossils

world_note: both bodies are C with no dependencies beyond libc; Techne's fossil-c-toolchain image serves both; a's parameters are compile-time so the four-error case needs only a driver, not a rebuild
